clue.text: Finished dealing? It won't stop here

parts.note: someone who is finished with something is through with it
dealing, especially in illicit goods, is trafficking or traffic

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a dealer has quit, then a sign says it won't stop here.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the first half as a playful reading of the answer's two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehicles passing through a place on their way elsewhere are the kind that do not halt there.

clue.text: Carpeting and doing well at the job

definitions.meaning: a carpeting is a severe telling-off, a reprimand
read literally, taking well to a task or piece of work

explanation.surface: A worker is both being reprimanded and performing well.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpeting is British slang for reprimanding, and to rebuke someone is to haul them over the coals.

clue.text: Cattle round-up was carried over

parts.note: to be carried on a horse is to have ridden, past tense rode
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A cattle round-up was moved on to another day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carried over' looks like postponed, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo began as a round-up of cattle in the American West, later a riding contest.

clue.text: Little cakes topped and iced with no training necessary

indicators.note: topped means having the top cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: buns are small sweet cakes
to ice someone is gangster slang for killing them

explanation.surface: Decorating small cakes with frosting needs no training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topped and iced' reads as cake decoration, but topped removes the first letter and iced means murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: Work needing no training is described as unskilled labour.

clue.text: Snobbish type going off before Derby, perhaps

parts.note: meat or game that is going off is said to be high
a derby is a bowler hat, one example of a hat

explanation.surface: A snob leaves early before the Derby horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous English horse race, but here a derby is the American word for a bowler hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-hat is a supercilious, haughty person who looks down on others.

clue.text: Root's declaring, with last pair going berserk

indicators.note: going wild signals the remaining letters are jumbled
the final two letters of the word declaring are the pair that go astray and drop out

explanation.surface: Joe Root's cricket declaration, with the last two batsmen going wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with last pair going' removes NG, leaving DECLARI, and 'going berserk' rearranges those letters. Joe Root is an England cricketer and a declaration ends an innings.
explanation.definitionFit: A radicle is the embryonic root of a plant, the first to emerge from a seed.

clue.text: Ultimately, if you sing, you make intricate music

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Sing well enough and you eventually produce elaborate music.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugue is a contrapuntal composition with interwoven voices repeating a theme.

clue.text: What's gathered within barrier engineers brought in

parts.note: within gives the synonym in

indicators.note: brought in means the engineers are placed inside the barrier

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers summoned inside a barrier to see what has been gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' here means understood, as in 'I gather', not collected.
explanation.definitionFit: A conclusion drawn from evidence is something one has gathered or deduced.

clue.text: Acclaim withdrawal of anti-Brit sentiment?

indicators.note: withdrawal means taking back, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: the curse 'Sod UK!' expresses hostility to Britain

explanation.surface: Is there praise for retracting hostility towards the British?
explanation.walkthrough: Taking back 'Sod UK!' turns its letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is praise and prestige earned for an achievement.

clue.text: He thinks he's Romeo, present on balcony

indicators.note: in an across clue on means the gift follows the balcony

parts.note: the gods is the highest balcony in a theatre
a present is a gift

explanation.surface: A would-be Romeo bearing a gift up on the balcony, as in Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: The Romeo and balcony picture evokes Shakespeare's play; the balcony is the theatre's gods.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who thinks himself irresistible is called God's gift to women, a vain ladies' man.

clue.text: "Goners' ledger" prepared here in London?

indicators.note: prepared means the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Where in London would a list of the dead be drawn up?
explanation.walkthrough: Golders Green, a north London district, is home to a well-known crematorium, so goners fit the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Golders Green is a district of north-west London, so it is a place in the capital.

clue.text: Tip of tool piercing irregular hole in ancient artefact

indicators.note: piercing means pushing a letter into the middle of the other letters
irregular indicates the letters are put out of order
the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sharp tool bores an uneven hole in a prehistoric object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hole in' is shuffled and the T from 'Tip of tool' goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A neolith is a stone implement from the New Stone Age, so an ancient relic.

clue.text: See you dispose of last two bits of Stilton, say, with port

indicators.text: dispose of last two bits of
indicators.note: the final two letters of the word are thrown away

parts.note: Stilton is an English blue cheese, an example of cheese
Rio de Janeiro, often just Rio, is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Finish the Stilton and the port, then say goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheese and port suggest the end of a dinner; port is the city, not the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British farewell, like saying goodbye until next time.

clue.text: Farmer's work clothes with durable fabric

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here, wrapping one piece around another

parts.note: to till is to plough land, a farmer's work

explanation.surface: A farmer's working clothes made with hard-wearing cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun for garments but is a verb meaning covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is a strong woven cloth with diagonal ribs, used for hardwearing garments.

clue.text: Like 10 and 27, not all recurring

indicators.note: not tells us to remove the following word from the longer one

parts.note: both linked answers have every word starting with G, so they are alliterative

explanation.surface: Two other answers share a pattern, though not every part repeats.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 and 27 are both all-G names, hence alliterative.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterative describes a process done repeatedly, each repetition recurring.

clue.text: Salesman wearing brown is bored in theatre

indicators.note: wearing means the brown piece is around the salesman

parts.note: suntanned skin is brown, or tanned
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A sun-browned salesman sits bored at a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bored in theatre' suggests a dull show but means drilled in an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To trepan is to drill a hole in the skull surgically, so a patient so treated was bored.

clue.text: Those deserving a lighter sentence?

parts.note: a lighter sentence sounds lenient, but these offenders use a lighter to start fires

explanation.surface: Which convicts merit a more lenient punishment?
explanation.definitionFit: People who deliberately set fires might, in jest, be sentenced by something that makes flames.

clue.text: On change of trade, factory offers tedious work

indicators.note: a change of the word means rearranging its letters

parts.note: a mill is a factory, as in a cotton mill

explanation.surface: After switching jobs, a factory offers only dull labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is any monotonous routine, from the wheel prisoners were made to walk.

clue.text: Cave in Spain, base for one male tramp

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the bottom, so Spain's letter goes below the rest

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to tramp is to walk heavily, to plod
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A cave in Spain serves as a home for a lone male vagrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave in' looks like a hollow somewhere in Spain but is a verb meaning collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: To implode is to collapse inwards, which is to fall in on itself.

clue.text: Devious fellow circumventing island's criminals

indicators.note: circumventing means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the island
devious means wandering off course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shifty man evades the crooks of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devious fellow' reads as a crook, but 'Devious' scrambles 'fellow' to LOWLFE, which goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowlife is a collective term for the criminal underworld and disreputable people.

clue.text: Female artist's backing cut

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: backing means turning the letters back to front

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A woman artist's financial support has been cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To shear is to clip or trim, as with sheep's wool.

clue.text: Seafood concession cut by demand

indicators.note: cut by means the first piece is split open with the second inside

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to placate someone
a call is a demand, as in calls on one's time

explanation.surface: A seafood stall's licence is cut short by public demand.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallop is a shellfish eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Future change required, with rise of pound

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise moves the letter higher, nearer the top

parts.note: to alter is to change
L stands for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Change is needed in future as the pound climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of pound' sounds like currency news but moves L upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Later as an adjective means subsequent, coming in the time ahead.

clue.text: He goes on to land after turning

indicators.note: after places the land piece after the turning piece

parts.note: winding is turning, as with a crank
to bag a prize is to land it

explanation.surface: A man continues travelling to reach land after changing direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes on' means talks endlessly, not travels onward.
explanation.definitionFit: A windbag is a tedious talker who rambles on at length.

clue.text: Subordinate to roar half-heartedly

indicators.note: half the heart goes, so one of the two central letters is dropped

parts.note: a bellow is a loud roar

explanation.surface: A junior officer shouts without real conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beneath someone in rank means lower down the order.

clue.text: Sporting tours hosted by seven star players

indicators.note: hosted by means held inside the seven

parts.note: VII is seven in Roman numerals

indicators.note: sporting suggests playing about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seven top sportsmen take part in sporting tours.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuosi are highly skilled performers, especially musicians.

clue.text: Local's first in to deliver soothing treatment

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the rescue verb

parts.note: to deliver from harm is to save

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word local

explanation.surface: A local's first job is to bring a calming remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A salve is an ointment that soothes wounds or sore skin.

clue.text: Best of United's wingers running round Hearts scorer?

parts.note: George Best was a star forward for Manchester United

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters surround the next piece
running suggests movement, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A Manchester United star's wide men run around Hearts, a Scottish club, looking for goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' suggests a goalscorer but means a writer of musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Gershwin composed scores such as Rhapsody in Blue, so he is a composer.
